info.name: LegiScore Partner API: guided flow
info.description:
The report flow, in the order you run it. Folders are numbered: work down them.

THE ONE THING TO KNOW
  The three enable*Review flags default to TRUE. With them on, a run pauses and waits for you
  indefinitely, there is no timeout and no auto-proceed. Use 2a for unattended runs.

SETUP
  1. Import this collection and its environment.
  2. Set api_key to your lsk_ key. base_url is preset to https://opinion.legiscore.in,
     and search_base_url to https://legiscore.in — folder 9 is a different product on a
     different host, sharing the same key.
  3. Run folders in order: 0 -> 1 -> 2a -> 3 (poll) -> 8.

Requests chain themselves: presign captures the upload URL, complete captures document_id,
create captures case_id. Run them in order and you never copy an id by hand.

Auth is collection-level: X-API-Key. (Authorization: Bearer <key> also works.)

Every endpoint, including the ones this flow does not use, is in the reference collection
alongside this file. That one is generated from the OpenAPI spec.

item.name: 0. Pre-flight
item.description: Run these two first. If either fails, stop — nothing downstream will work.

request.description:
Confirms three things at once: your key is valid, it is bound to your organisation, and the org wallet has credits. A report costs 1 credit.

If this 401s, the key is wrong. If the balance looks like a personal wallet rather than the org's, the key is not org-bound — tell us and we'll fix it.
Optional. Shows the custom-field schemas configured for your org.

item.name: 1. Upload the document
item.description:
Three calls: ask for a signed URL, PUT the bytes straight to storage, then tell us it landed.

IMPORTANT: 1b must fully finish (200) before you call 1c. Calling 1c early returns 422 object_not_found — that is the single most common integration mistake.

request.description:
fileSize must be the real byte count. The returned uploadUrl expires in 60 minutes.

Saves uploadUrl + objectName into the environment.

Select your file under Body > binary before sending.

Two rules: the Content-Type here MUST match what you sent in 1a, and you must wait for the 200 before calling 1c.

This goes directly to object storage — it does not pass through our API, so your key is not sent here.

exec: pm.test('Upload returned 200 — safe to call 1c now', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

request.description:
Registers the uploaded object as a document and returns document_id.

422 object_not_found here means the PUT in 1b had not finished. Wait and retry — do not re-presign.

item.name: 2. Create the report
item.description:
Pick ONE of these two. They differ only in the three review flags.

READ THIS: the three enable*Review flags DEFAULT TO TRUE if you omit them. With them on, the run pauses and waits for you — it will not finish on its own, ever. There is no timeout. Use 2a unless you are deliberately driving the checkpoints.

header.description: Retry-safe: same key + same body returns the original response instead of creating a duplicate case.

request.description:
Uses the {{documentId}} collection variable. It ships empty: run folder 1 first and 1c fills it in for you, or paste in a document id you already hold.

All three review flags OFF. The run goes end to end unattended and reaches completed with no further calls from you. This is what you want for automated/LOS-driven volume.

documentIds MUST be an array, even for one document.

Charges 1 credit from your organisation's wallet at creation.

item.name: 2b. Interactive (checkpoints ON — you must drive folders 4/5/6)

request.description:
Uses the {{documentId}} collection variable. It ships empty: run folder 1 first and 1c fills it in for you, or paste in a document id you already hold.

All three review flags ON. The run will PAUSE up to three times and sit in awaiting_review until you call the matching resume endpoint in folders 4, 5 and 6.

If you only poll /status and never resume, this case never completes.

Poll every 15–30s. Read the `state` field — it is a stable 5-value vocabulary:

  queued      — accepted, not started
  running     — processing
  awaiting_review — PAUSED at a checkpoint; read internal_status to see which
  completed   — done, call folder 7
  failed      — terminal

A straight-through run typically takes several minutes.

This call is free and side-effect free.

exec: console.log('PAUSED — resume via folder 4/5/6 depending on internal_status');

item.name: 4. Checkpoint 1 — Document analysis
item.description:
CHECKPOINT 1 — DOCUMENT ANALYSIS

YOU ARE HERE WHEN:
  GET /api/cases/{id}/status returns
      "state":           "awaiting_review"
      "internal_status": "awaiting_document_review"
  (webhook equivalent: event report.paused.review, data.stage = "document_review")

WHAT PAUSED, IN PLAIN TERMS:
  We have read your documents and pulled out the key facts — document number, date,
  parties, survey number, house number. We are showing you what we extracted before we
  spend money running government searches against it. A wrong survey number here means
  every search downstream is wrong.

HOW TO PROCEED — two ways:

  (a) Accept the extraction as-is  [most common]
      POST /api/cases/{id}/submit-document-review
      { "updates": [], "proceed_to_searches": true }

  (b) Correct something first
      POST /api/cases/{id}/submit-document-review
      { "updates": [
          { "document_id": "<from 4a>", "field_name": "survey_number", "new_value": "21/A" }
        ],
        "proceed_to_searches": true }

      field_name must be one of the editable_fields returned by 4a:
      document_number, document_date, parties, survey_number, house_number

AFTER THIS: state returns to "running" and external searches begin.

request.description: Returns the extracted fields per document plus editable_fields.

Send updates: [] to accept the AI extraction as-is.

To correct a field: {"document_id": "...", "field_name": "survey_number", "new_value": "21/A"} — field_name must be one of editable_fields from 4a.

item.name: 5. Checkpoint 2 — Missing documents
item.description:
CHECKPOINT 2 — MISSING DOCUMENTS

YOU ARE HERE WHEN:
  GET /api/cases/{id}/status returns
      "state":           "awaiting_review"
      "internal_status": "awaiting_documents"
  (webhook equivalent: event report.paused.missing_documents, data.stage = "missing_documents")

WHAT PAUSED, IN PLAIN TERMS:
  The analysis found the title chain needs documents you have not given us — typically an
  Encumbrance Certificate or a parent/link deed. You decide: supply them, or go ahead
  without them and let the report record the gap.

HOW TO PROCEED — three ways:

  (a) Go ahead without them  [the unattended default]
      POST /api/cases/{id}/continue
      { "new_document_ids": [], "proceed_anyway": true }
      The report is produced and states what was missing.

  (b) Supply the missing documents
      1. Upload each one through folder 1 (presign -> PUT -> complete)
      2. POST /api/cases/{id}/continue
         { "new_document_ids": ["<new document_id>"], "proceed_anyway": false }

  (c) Supply them AND say which gap each one fills  [optional, most precise]
      1. Upload through folder 1
      2. PATCH /api/cases/{id}/missing-documents/{slot_index}/link
         { "document_ids": ["<new document_id>"] }
         slot_index = 0-based position in the missing_documents[] array from 5a
      3. POST /api/cases/{id}/continue  { "new_document_ids": [], "proceed_anyway": false }

NOTE: 5a returns iteration / max_iterations. We can ask more than once (up to 3 rounds) as
new documents reveal new gaps.

RETURNS 400 if the case is not actually awaiting documents — check status first.

request.description: Returns missing_documents[] plus iteration / max_iterations.

item.name: 5b. Link an uploaded doc to a slot (optional)

request.description: Optional. Upload the new document via folder 1 first, then attach it to a specific missing-document slot. slot_index is the 0-based position in missing_documents[] from 5a.

proceed_anyway: true continues without supplying the remaining documents — the report will say what was missing.

To supply them instead: upload via folder 1, then pass the ids in new_document_ids and set proceed_anyway: false.

Returns 400 if the case is not actually awaiting documents.

item.name: 6. Checkpoint 3 — Risk acknowledgement
item.description:
CHECKPOINT 3 — RISK ACKNOWLEDGEMENT

YOU ARE HERE WHEN:
  GET /api/cases/{id}/status returns
      "state":           "awaiting_review"
      "internal_status": "awaiting_acknowledgements"
  (webhook equivalent: event report.paused.acknowledgements, data.stage = "acknowledgements")

WHAT PAUSED, IN PLAIN TERMS:
  The diligence found risks on the title. Before we issue the report, someone on your side
  has to say, on the record, that your credit team accepts them. This is the last gate.

HOW TO PROCEED:

  POST /api/cases/{id}/submit-acknowledgements
  { "acknowledgements": [
      { "id": "risk_1", "decision": "accepted", "bypass_reason": "Accepted by credit team" },
      { "id": "risk_2", "decision": "rejected", "bypass_reason": "Not acceptable to credit" }
    ] }

  One entry per risk returned by 6a. Send each item back WHOLE — spread the object 6a gave
  you and add the decision — because a field you drop is a field the report loses.

    decision: "accepted"    your team accepts this risk, proceed
    decision: "rejected"    not accepted — it stays flagged in the report
    decision: "undecided"   no call made on it yet

  An item sent with NO decision acknowledges nothing, so a case can look answered when
  nothing was actually decided.

  Do not send is_bypassed yourself. The server derives it from decision, and sending both
  is rejected when they disagree.

  bypass_reason is written into the report verbatim. Make it something you would be
  comfortable showing an auditor.

READ THIS BEFORE AUTOMATING IT:
  This call creates a legal acceptance record, attributed to whoever's API key made it.
  Do not blanket-accept every risk from a script. If your process is that a human approves,
  that human's decision should be what drives this call.

AFTER THIS: state returns to "running" and final report generation starts.

request.description: Returns the risk points raised during analysis.

One entry per risk from 6a, sent back whole with a decision added: "accepted", "rejected" or "undecided". An item with no decision acknowledges nothing. Do not set is_bypassed — the server derives it from decision, and sending both is rejected when they disagree. bypass_reason is recorded in the report verbatim.

This is a legal acceptance record — it is attributed to whoever's key made the call.

Submitting launches final report generation.

item.name: 7. Event-driven mode (instead of polling)
item.description:
WHERE THE WEBHOOK URL GOES: NOWHERE IN YOUR CALLS.
This is the one piece of the integration you never send on a request. You give us the URL
once, we store it against your API key, and from then on WE call YOU. The
{{your_webhook_url}} environment variable exists only so the example below renders — it is
never a body field and never a header.

TO TURN IT ON: register the endpoint yourself with POST /api/v1/webhooks (client.webhooks in
either SDK), or send us the URL and we will register it for you. The signing secret comes back
exactly once, at create or rotate — store it then, because nothing can read it back.

WHY BOTHER: it replaces folder 3. Instead of polling, you get told the moment a run pauses
or finishes — and told exactly WHICH checkpoint paused, so you know which call to make next.

EVENT -> data.stage -> the call you make:
  report.paused.review            -> document_review   -> folder 4  submit-document-review
  report.paused.missing_documents -> missing_documents -> folder 5  continue
  report.paused.acknowledgements  -> acknowledgements  -> folder 6  submit-acknowledgements
  report.completed                -> -                 -> folder 8  result
  report.failed                   -> -                 -> stop

Every pause callback carries, under data:
  stage            which checkpoint (the 3 values above)
  state            always "awaiting_review"
  internal_status  the precise internal status
  pause_reason     short category line, never empty
  pause_detail     full remark with counts and specifics, never empty
  metadata         your own correlation blob, echoed back verbatim

Signed with X-LegiScore-Signature (HMAC-SHA256 over timestamp + body) and retried on failure.
We can also map the payload field-by-field into your own schema so it arrives shaped like
your objects rather than ours — we configure that on our side.

item.name: 7a. Example pause callback WE would POST to YOU

request.description:
Reference only — do not send this. This is the shape WE post to YOUR url.

Read data.stage, call the matching resume endpoint from folder 4/5/6, done. Your metadata rides along so you never need a case-id mapping table.
The structured report — findings, risks, title chain, custom fields, LegiScore. This is the machine-readable deliverable and what you map into your own system.
Lists the uploaded documents, everything added during review, and the raw government-search artifacts.
Same set as 7b, streamed as a single ZIP.

The rendered, branded report document.

NOTE: this is a separate endpoint from /files — the ZIP and file list deliberately do NOT include the rendered report. Uploads and search artifacts come from 7b/7c; the document comes from here.

Use Send and Download in Postman to save the file.

item.name: 9. Government record searches
item.description:
A separate product from the report flow, and it does not share its money.

  * Different host. Every request here uses {{search_base_url}}, not {{base_url}}.
  * Different credits. 9b reads them; the report balance in folder 0 is a different pot.
  * Flat price per search, stated by 9a. Charged when a search is accepted and returned
    if the source cannot be reached.

Run 9a to see what can be searched, 9c to turn a name into the codes a search needs,
then 9d -> 9e -> 9g. A succeeded search with found=false is an answer: the source was
reached and holds nothing against that property.

item.name: 9a. Catalog — what can be searched, and what it costs

request.description:
Every live state, the search types in it, the fields each one takes and the current price per search. Needs no key, so it is the one request here you can run before you have one.

Read the price from this response. Do not hardcode it.

source.status says whether the government source is reachable right now. When it is unavailable, searches will not consume credits: the charge is reversed the moment a job fails to reach the portal.

The search balance, what is spendable right now, and the recent movements against it.

This is NOT the balance folder 0 shows. A run of searches can never spend the credits bought to generate reports, and vice versa. If this 401s while folder 0 passes, your network reaches one host and not the other.

item.name: 9c. Lookups — turn a name into the codes a search needs

request.description:
Lookup fields are picked, never typed. 9a names the dimension each field uses (sro, district, mandal, village and the rest); this returns the valid options for one of them.

Send the option's value AND spread its meta into params — those are the codes the source actually keys on. A nested dimension needs its parent first: ask for a village with district and mandal already chosen, or you get missing_parent.

Fill state, search_type and params from 9a and 9c, then send. 202 means accepted, not finished — poll 9e.

For a batch, replace the body with {"searches": [ ... ]}, up to 25. A batch runs the items that validated: read `rejected`, which names the index of each one that did not, and `credits_charged` for what the call actually spent.

402 with code insufficient_credits means top up; nothing was charged.
replayed counts the searches answered from an identical run of yours in the last 24 hours, which cost nothing and never touched the source.

exec: pm.test('at least one search started', () => pm.expect(first).to.be.an('object'));

request.description:
Repeat until status is succeeded, failed or cancelled. 9a's typical_seconds tells you how long to expect; every few seconds is a sensible interval.

found=false on a SUCCEEDED search is an answer, not an error: the source was reached and holds nothing against that property. Do not retry it.

status awaiting_otp means the source asked for a one-time password; POST it to /api/v1/search/{{search_id}}/otp. Most searches never reach that state.

exec: console.log('Status:', s.status, '| found:', s.found, '| records:', s.record_count);

request.description:
Newest first. Anything still in flight is refreshed on the way past, so a list call doubles as a poll for a whole batch.

Add status= to filter, or batch_id= to see only the searches one submit started.

The filename comes from 9e's documents list; 9e captures the first one into search_document for you.

This answers 302 with a signed URL that expires in an hour. Postman follows redirects by default and will show you the file. If you are writing the call yourself, do NOT follow the redirect on the same connection: your API key is a custom header, and custom headers are forwarded across a cross-origin redirect. Read the Location header and fetch it with no key attached. Both SDKs already do this.

The file is looked up in the search's own document list, so a filename that is not on this search is 404.

variable.description: A document id to create a case from. Ships empty. Folder 1c fills it in for you, or paste in an id you already hold.
A filename from a search's documents list. Ships empty. Request 9e fills it in for you.
